prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the foreground road and people from the more distant tractor, loaded trailer, wall, buildings, and trees: the closest person is roughly 1–2 m from the camera, the tractor about 3–5 m away, the trailer about 4–7 m away, and the background mostly beyond 8 m. Across the five frames, the nearby person shifts from near the centre-left to the right edge and becomes partly cropped, while another person carrying a large object enters close in front, passes through the centre-right at roughly 1–2 m, and then moves leftward relative to the camera view. The tractor remains left of the trailer, with their overlapping silhouettes showing that the tractor is nearer in the image where one blocks part of the other; trees and overhead lines lie above and well behind both vehicles. Bright foreground silhouettes make proximity and occlusion easier to see than in RGB alone, but the map has holes in foliage and people, merges nearby surfaces at similar depths, and provides only rough metric distances.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies several people, the tractor-like vehicle as “motorcycle,” the loaded trailer as “truck,” and the large carried object in later frames as “surfboard,” exposing object boundaries and overlaps that are less distinct in RGB. It shows people positioned beside or in front of the vehicles: early people overlap the tractor and trailer masks, while in later frames a foreground person overlaps the carried-object mask and partly blocks more distant people and vehicles. The foreground person and carried object are within roughly arm’s reach of each other and about 1–2 m from the camera; the vehicles are several metres farther away, although segmentation itself does not directly encode distance. Across the strip, masks shift from the left and centre toward the right as the camera turns, with some people entering or leaving the frame and the final foreground person cut off by the right boundary. Reliability is limited by incorrect class labels, fragmented or missing masks, duplicate person labels, and inconsistent coverage of partially occluded bodies and objects.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only two sparse yellow upper-body or arm configurations in the middle-late frames, placing the detected person in front of the camera around the centre-right and then farther right as the viewpoint changes. The connected joints indicate a bent arm held below the head, but the skeleton is too incomplete to determine full-body orientation, exact facing direction, gaze toward the camera, or reliable reach relationships. Compared with RGB, it makes the detected joint arrangement and its frame-to-frame lateral shift easier to isolate against the scene, while showing that no confident body or hand pose was recovered in most frames. It is highly unreliable here because it misses several clearly visible people, produces no magenta hand skeletons, omits legs and much of the torso, and cannot represent the surrounding vehicles, distances, or occlusions.
